title: EvaluationResult
description: The result of one residual evaluation (plan §2.1, §2.2 P02/K01 row; frozen in docs/interfaces-frozen.md §1). Carries status, values, phase signature, the identity of the state and the problem, evaluation counters and accuracy. Three rules a JSON Schema cannot express are checked by tests/test_k01_schemas.py: `values` must be present and the same length as `equation_ids` when and only when `status` is `ok`; a decoded NaN or infinity satisfies `type: number` but is not a value this boundary may report as `ok`; and `state_sha256` must be the canonical hash of the `x` that produced it, which only the evaluator can know.

values.description: Residual values in `equation_ids` order, or null. Null is the honest report for any status other than `ok`: an unevaluated residual is absent, never zeros.

model_version.description: Format `<label>@<structure_sha256>` (ADR 0002 D2.3): the label names the function family and the 64 hex characters are the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the structure document — variable_ids, equation_ids, parameter_ids and row_accumulation. The compiler assigns it; a reader recomputes it where the document carries those lists.

state_sha256.description: Hash of exactly the dense `x` as passed, in `variable_ids` order, after signed-zero normalization, and nothing else (ADR 0008 D2). No context field, no time, no pseudo-time and no integrator internal participates.

message.description: Why, when the status is not `ok`. Empty otherwise. A blocked or out-of-domain evaluation says so here rather than returning a number.

status.description: `invalid_trial_state` means the state left a declared domain and the solver should shorten its step; `unsupported` means the capability does not exist, which is never a silent success.

counters.description: Per-block call accounting, `{block_id: {counter: count}}` (ADR 0003 D5.5). `n_inputs + 1` value calls per Jacobian is the finite-difference signature, so this is evidence rather than telemetry.
